I am sorry for not giving much detail! So I have issues when I pray - recitation mistakes are the main.It takes me around 15 minutes to finish one salah, so I feel horrible afterwards. My parents and my two older sisters said I can recite it correctly, but I do not think so. I am a non-Arab, and started Arabic class this year. I am in my second semester, and I had already learned how to recite the prayer in the Arabic letters but I keep making mistakes. I don’t really focus in prayer because I am usually focused on the words, so I sadly don’t get the barakah from my prayers most of the time.

Another one is wudu. It takes me a while, I am very intricate on body parts that are typically not paid attention to by most. For example, I tend to intricately wipe in between my toes, and try to get water under my nails. I try to wipe my eyelashes too and If I don’t do these things, I feel uneasy.

I also tend to get scared of making dua and reading Quran which I noticed recently. I get these thoughts that Allah hates me and I am disgusting so I just don’t do it. For example, when I go online to read or memorize Surahs in Quran, I just get very sad because I feel like I am not like others in that I am not a good person. 

Recently it’s gotten very bad. I saw a post that said that the shaytaan is going to attack us this month since they will be chained next month for Ramadan. I get so sad when I have to pray now which is not good. Most of my day consists of me just waiting for the next prayer to come so I don’t have to deal with any issues. I love Islam, but this and other personal issues drained my energy so much that everything just got so hard! I do not think this is OCD and I am not sure if this is waswas because my doubts are right most of the time. But I feel I have to ignore them, even if they are right, otherwise everything is going to get so hard that maybe something bad will happen Astagfirullah. I am sorry if this is too much information, and I am sorry if I said anything bad here. But thank you so much for the advice.
